policy: Only the bounded original passage claims are checked. The label original scope checked must not mean full eight-stage verification; source role and limitations remain explicit. Original opponent excerpts in hostile CDF notification are not whole-book independent collation.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Pius XII explicitly treats consecrated virginity as a freely chosen vocation for God's kingdom and rebuts the notion that permanent continence is inherently impossible.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The encyclical does not establish an empirical psychological superiority of all celibates, nor classify clinical distress.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The argument supports the possibility and dignity of consecrated chastity without redefining marriage as evil.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It cannot supply incidence, causality or population estimates for psychological distress in Catholic priests.

records.passage_locator: 1986 letter, list of contested sexual-morality positions
records.what_original_establishes_en: The CDF correspondence actually discusses Charles Curran's disputed teaching in sexual morality, establishing the wider historical debate.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not articulate the claim that engaged partners already have matrimonial sexual rights or that a wedding is merely ornamental.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Casti Connubii understands marriage as a real covenant with duties of fidelity and an objective order to generation and education.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not address a contemporary engaged-couple contraception scenario in the specific wording used by this stage.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas analyzes scandal in relation to conduct that gives another a spiritual stumbling block; scandal is not identical to whether two people occupy one residence.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The article neither automatically condemns every chaste house-sharing arrangement nor empirically establishes cohabitation outcomes.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas's account of fornication links sexual relations to stable responsibility for children, which supplies a reason for marriage preceding sexual union.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: He does not conduct comparative research into premarital cohabitation or establish the risk-reduction efficacy of any particular courtship practice.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Christ identifies intentionally lustful looking as an interior moral act and not simply the external act of adultery.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The verse does not state that noticing attractiveness without consent is sinful or specify a precise time threshold for an intentional gaze.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas distinguishes an act's object and circumstances in moral assessment, supporting a distinction between spontaneous attraction and chosen indulgence.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: He gives no empirical test by which an observer could measure another person's internal consent from a glance.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Christ's teaching concerns voluntary interior lust; it provides the general basis for considering chosen intentions alongside physical conduct.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The text does not define all dating boundaries, flirtation or an exclusive-boyfriend agreement as objectively equivalent to adultery.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas distinguishes the object and circumstances of human choices, allowing honest assessment of what a particular interpersonal action seeks.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The article does not condemn every smile, compliment, attraction or ambiguous social exchange as disloyal flirtation.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas explicitly holds that kisses and touches are not mortally sinful by their species in every case; purpose and knowingly chosen pleasure matter.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: This does not license deliberate acts of genital stimulation outside marriage, nor establish that every affectionate gesture is prudent.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Persona Humana affirms the moral reservation of sexual union to marriage and treats deliberately chosen sexual pleasure as having an objective moral context.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The declaration does not provide a complete moral taxonomy of every contemporary non-intercourse technique; the particulars remain a further moral analysis.

records.passage_locator: Farley Just Love pp.293, 295 quoted in CDF Notification (2012)
records.what_original_establishes_en: The CDF notification reproduces Farley's own defense of legal recognition and sexual-ethical evaluation of same-sex relationships.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The cited document is an adversarial official response reproducing selected excerpts, not independent collation of her full original book.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The CDF document sets out the Roman Catholic distinction between matrimonial union and legal recognition of same-sex unions.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not dispute the factual possibility of enduring love or sacrifice in same-sex partnerships; the argument concerns what marriage is.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Canon 1084 explicitly says that sterility does not prevent or nullify a marriage, while addressing perpetual impotence separately.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The objection inferring legal recognition of same-sex unions from that difference is illustrative and not authored by the Code or by Farley.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The Code supplies the actual legal distinction: antecedent perpetual impotence is an impediment; sterility alone is not.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not itself demonstrate every claim about the metaphysics of generative-type union or conclude the dispute about same-sex marriage.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Pius XI treats procreation and formation of children as marriage goods and also expressly affirms conjugal honor, mutual fidelity and spousal love.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The passage does not reduce marriage to successful childbirth or treat childless couples as invalidly married.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The encyclical teaches both the education of children and a sustained faithful, chaste and loving conjugal partnership.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not amount to an empirical survey of why contemporary couples marry or the precise happiness of every childless marriage.

records.passage_locator: Farley Just Love pp.304–305 excerpted in CDF Notification
records.what_original_establishes_en: Farley actually discusses conditions under which the moral commitment of marriage may be released, as quoted by the CDF.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: Her excerpts do not literally assert that every unhappy marriage should be dissolved or that abuse and ordinary incompatibility are interchangeable.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Pius XI treats the bond and its indissolubility as doctrinal matters, including the distinction from mere civil divorce.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: These paragraphs do not order vulnerable spouses to remain in dangerous cohabitation; concrete protective separation is provided for in later canon law.

records.passage_locator: Farley Just Love p.310 excerpted in CDF Notification
records.what_original_establishes_en: Farley gives a genuine dissenting treatment of divorce and remarriage, so this objection has an actual opposing author behind its general concern.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The precise 'innocent spouse is punished' rhetorical sentence remains an editorial reconstruction, not a demonstrated quotation from Farley.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Canon law distinguishes an existing bond and impediment to a second marriage from declarations of invalidity and exceptional dissolution provisions.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The legal categories do not establish that every particular nullity decree was correct; the case requires competent tribunal evaluation.

records.passage_locator: Supplement q.64 a.1, replies to objections 2–3
records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas does assert reciprocal marital duties but expressly limits what may be required by the spouse's wellbeing, rejecting unjust exactions.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The historical treatise does not give a modern criminal-law consent standard and does not imply a right to forced intercourse.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Canon 1153 provides grounds for separation where serious danger to the spouse or children makes common living unsafe and addresses urgent departure.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not create a right to coerce sexual acts; nor does separating itself automatically dissolve a valid marriage.

records.passage_locator: Farley Just Love p.236 quoted in CDF Notification
records.what_original_establishes_en: The original author excerpt evaluates masturbation under a relational-welfare justice framework rather than treating the act as intrinsically immoral.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It is not the entire book and does not justify inferring that Farley explicitly dismisses all objective moral duties.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Persona Humana distinguishes the objectively disordered character of masturbation from diminished voluntariness due to habit, anxiety or immaturity.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: The declaration does not state that every occurrence constitutes mortal personal guilt or that third-party harm is the sole moral criterion.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The Catechism's definition of pornography names real or simulated sexual acts displayed deliberately to third parties and identifies dignity concerns.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not claim that lack of consent is the only wrong or pronounce an empirical finding about prevalence of trafficking.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Section 2354 condemns deliberate third-party display of sexual acts and treats it as morally significant beyond the question of performer consent.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: Its definition should not be silently extended to every nude portrait, private spousal recording or nonexplicit representation.

records.what_original_establishes_en: Aquinas distinguishes an act's object, circumstances and intention; this allows different moral cases to be assessed without assuming identical classification.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: Aquinas does not discuss photographs, encrypted files, or private spousal recordings, so any direct prohibition would be an anachronism.

records.what_original_establishes_en: The Catechism's pornography rule explicitly concerns displaying sexual acts to third parties and is not a general rule about every digital medium.
records.what_it_does_not_establish_en: It does not settle the prudence of private spousal images or their retention, dissemination risk or moral classification without further argument.
